Real-time AI

Building a voice AI system where latency is part of the product.

A conversational voice application: speech recognition, LLM inference, and speech synthesis, orchestrated asynchronously over WebSockets. In voice, a fraction of a second is the difference between a conversation and a chore — so the system was designed around the latency budget from the start.

Problem

Three slow operations in sequence — hear, think, speak — with a human waiting on the other end. Run them one after another and the conversation feels broken. The product only works if the whole pipeline fits inside a latency budget a person finds natural.

Approach

The pipeline runs asynchronously over WebSockets: recognition, inference, and synthesis overlap instead of waiting on each other. Each stage is monitored like infrastructure — in a real-time system, a slow stage is a product defect.

Outcome

A voice system that holds a natural conversation. Built like infrastructure, monitored like infrastructure, with latency treated as a feature rather than a number on a dashboard.

Latency designed in, not measured after.
